<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/sharing_rule.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f27464b7de65d55c42ed0195f42a3b346a38dc48` — the merge of head `63417d56d5216bbcf5dc0355fbe4915aad2f7dc5` into base `dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f27464b7de65d55c42ed0195f42a3b346a38dc48 && git checkout f27464b7de65d55c42ed0195f42a3b346a38dc48
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42 63417d56d5216bbcf5dc0355fbe4915aad2f7dc5 && git checkout -B drift-repro dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42 && git merge --no-ff 63417d56d5216bbcf5dc0355fbe4915aad2f7dc5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dbca3ef034537269cef482b342aa4ba7169dfe42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The refusal is one gating registry rule, `title-format-retired` (`CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, object), which `os validate`, build, lint and the save gate all run. The 68 system objects drop the key, as the claim's "every `titleFormat` hit" asks. The PR body names the nine forced test edits; the 60 → 61 author-time rule count appears in four doc transcripts. All are accepted.

### ① Derived judgments

**Branch delta integrity — intact.** Round-1 delta (`925e86070c...0885931864`) and round-2 delta (`86d36e9974...986011757d`, the new merge base) carry the same 101-file list; a per-file comparison of the hunks (headers and index lines stripped) differs in exactly five files: the changeset and the four transcripts, i.e. the two fixes. `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` and `references/system/migration.mdx` were regenerated from the merged tree (`75c2ac28a8`, +8/−4) and their branch-attributable hunks are byte-equal to round 1; the extra lines are main-side describe changes the regeneration absorbed. The merge commit brings 281 main-side files and drops or alters no branch change.

**(A) Transcripts — correct on the head, stale against `main` again.** Measured by counting `name:` entries inside `AUTHORING_RULES` (every entry's `commands` includes `validate`, so `authoringRulesFor('validate').length` equals the entry count): merge base `86d36e9974` = 61, head = 62, and the four transcripts on the head read 62 (`deployment/cli.mdx:774`, `deployment/validating-metadata.mdx:763`, `getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx:313`, `ui/react-pages.mdx:407`). The drift gate (`check:docs-transcript-drift`, lint.yml job `Type Check · workspace`) is green on this head. But `origin/main` (`ebbb5b8867`) has since landed #29495 (`7f368f56ec`, `validateFlowRegionShape`) with its own 61 → 62 edit to the same four lines: `main` = 62 rules / transcripts 62; head = 62 / 62; the merged tree = 63 rules (union of the two added names) while the three-way merge of identical textual edits leaves the transcripts at 62. The gate runs on `merge_group`, so the queue reds the merge result exactly as in round 1. **MUST-FIX A′**: merge `origin/main` once more and set the four transcripts to 63 — or to whatever the union count is at the moment of the merge — and queue immediately. This is the same race twice in one day: four hand-written literals that every rule-adding PR edits; a card on the gate (regenerate the count in the queue leg, or stop printing a literal) is owed, not this PR's.

**(B) Kind line — half landed.** `.changeset/29007-object-title-format-refused.md:20` now reads `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` beside `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the `registered object-title-format-refused` marker. The PR body as served on `986011757d` still reads `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, and its Verification bullet still says the offline gate "accepts `no (narrowing)` with `semantic`". The level gate reads the kind from the PR body ("declared ONCE, FOR THE PR — a PR-body line"), so the declaration of record is still the wrong one; no gate cross-checks the body line against the changeset line (the "disagree" refusal is declaration-vs-level, not body-vs-changeset), which is why `Check Changeset` is green either way. **MUST-FIX B (remaining)**: patch the PR body to `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and reword the Verification bullet; the dev reports this as owed.
